t: This is Tooley Street, a road running from London Bridge towards St Saviour's Dock, passing Tower Bridge on the Southwark and Bermondsey side of the river. Its name is a worn-down form of Saint Olaf, the Norwegian king who ruled from 1015 to 1028 and was later made a saint. It is also tied to James Braidwood, the first director of the London Fire Engine Establishment, who died here. He is credited with developing the modern municipal fire service.
